summary: The bill exempts commercial motor vehicles transporting livestock, insects, or aquatic animals from federal hours-of-service limits and electronic logging device requirements, including when unladen before pickup or after delivery.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates no new government programs, appropriations, or changes to federal spending levels. It is purely a regulatory exemption for certain commercial vehicles.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection of any kind.
The legislation has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the text.
The bill does not address immigration, visas, border policy, or related enforcement.

The bill explicitly exempts covered vehicles from electronic logging device (ELD) mandates under 49 U.S.C. § 31137. This constitutes a reduction in federal technology-based regulatory requirements for a specific industry sector.

The core of the bill is an exemption from hours-of-service rules (subchapter III of chapter 311 and chapter 315 of title 49). These rules are longstanding federal labor/safety protections limiting driver work time. Removing them increases employer operational flexibility in the livestock transport sector.
No content addresses religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
